subject: /knowledge/claude-code-hooks/subagentstart-envelope
body: SubagentStart delivers additionalContext only via the hookSpecificOutput envelope; bare stdout is silently discarded even though SessionStart accepts it.

subject: /knowledge/claude-code-hooks/subagentstart-scope
body: SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, and Stop hooks never fire for a subagent; only PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied, and SubagentStart do.

subject: /knowledge/claude-code-hooks/agent-id-discriminator
body: agent_id present in a hook payload is the reliable subagent discriminator; agent_type alone is not, since it is also set on a top-level --agent session.

subject: /knowledge/claude-code-hooks/agent-type-key-name
body: The subagent's type is keyed agent_type on SubagentStart but subagent_type inside PreToolUse's tool_input; reading the wrong key name matches nothing, silently.

subject: /knowledge/claude-code-hooks/pretooluse-exit-codes
body: PreToolUse exit code 0 allows, 2 denies and feeds stderr back to the model, but 1 is an error and not a block — it is silently treated as allow.

subject: /knowledge/claude-code-hooks/temporal-dead-zone
body: A const referenced from an early-returning branch but declared later in the file throws ReferenceError at runtime, not at node --check, silently disabling the whole guard since exit 1 is not a block.

subject: /knowledge/claude-code-hooks/plugin-cache-pinning
body: Editing a plugin's hook files in a marketplace working tree has no effect; the loaded copy is cached per plugin version and only refreshes when the plugin's version number bumps.

subject: /knowledge/claude-code-hooks/sessionend-timeout
body: SessionEnd enforces a very short timeout, about 1.5s observed; real work must be backgrounded with stdin captured first or it is killed mid-flight.

subject: /knowledge/claude-code-hooks/precompact-budget
body: PreCompact is budgeted generously, 90s in one observed config, so heavier synchronous work is affordable there, unlike SessionEnd.

subject: /knowledge/claude-code-hooks/precompact-no-injection
body: PreCompact has no additionalContext injection channel; its decision:block refuses the compaction outright rather than annotating it, so it cannot inject context.

subject: /knowledge/claude-code-hooks/subagentstart-reach
body: To get a directive into every subagent, including workflow-spawned ones, use SubagentStart — a PreToolUse rewrite of the Agent tool's input cannot reach them; a measured 47-agent run confirmed zero relay events that way.

subject: /knowledge/claude-code-hooks/hook-context-aggregation
body: additionalContext from multiple hooks on one event aggregates safely, but conflicting permissionDecision values across hooks on the same event are undocumented — let only one plugin deny a given tool.

subject: /knowledge/claude-code-hooks/no-agent-roster-at-spawn
body: A subagent cannot see the available-agent roster until the result of its own first tool call; a directive naming an unresolvable agent type fails silently and looks identical to the subagent ignoring it.

subject: /knowledge/claude-code-hooks/plugin-agent-type-match
body: Plugin agent types are namespaced as plugin:agent, so match them anchored, (^|:)name$, never by bare name, or a same-named agent from another plugin will match too.

subject: /knowledge/claude-code-hooks/hook-payload-no-tier
body: Hook payloads carry no model or capability-tier field; effort is a thinking-level setting, not a model tier, so tier-based routing needs another signal.

subject: /knowledge/claude-code-hooks/subagentstart-envelope-keys
body: All three SubagentStart envelope keys are load-bearing and hookEventName must exactly match the firing event, or the additionalContext is not delivered.

subject: /knowledge/claude-code-hooks/additionalcontext-size
body: A ~7.5 KB additionalContext payload was delivered untruncated in a live SubagentStart probe; do not assume a truncation threshold exists without testing one.

subject: /knowledge/plugin-conventions/hook-toggle-mechanism
body: A hook's on/off toggle is handled by a script that checks enabled state at run time, not by editing settings.json to add or remove the hook entry.

subject: /knowledge/plugin-conventions/toggle-state-shape
body: Toggle state is a JSON config with an explicit enabled boolean, not a marker file's mere existence — presence on disk and what status reports can drift apart.

subject: /knowledge/plugin-conventions/plugin-state-location
body: Plugin state lives in the user's own Claude config directory, not inside the version-pinned plugin cache, so it survives the plugin's auto-updates.

subject: /knowledge/plugin-conventions/concurrent-write-log-format
body: Concurrent-write state files are append-only JSONL, never read-modify-write — read-modify-write under concurrency measurably dropped roughly 4 of 12 writes.

subject: /knowledge/plugin-conventions/log-pruning-pattern
body: Log pruning writes a pid-suffixed temp file first, then atomically renames it over the original, rather than truncating or rewriting the log in place.

subject: /knowledge/plugin-conventions/hook-enabled-check-order
body: Hooks check whether they are enabled via a cheap unlocked read before taking any lock or doing real work, so a disabled hook costs almost nothing.

subject: /knowledge/plugin-conventions/hook-failure-isolation
body: Hook bodies are wrapped in try/catch and exit 0 on failure, so a broken hook never blocks the tool call or session it is attached to.

subject: /knowledge/plugin-conventions/blocking-gate-fail-open
body: A blocking gate hook fails open on its own internal error, rather than blocking the user's work because the gate itself broke.

subject: /knowledge/plugin-conventions/toggle-scope-targeting
body: On/off toggles target the narrowest scope that already has a config file, so a repo-level opt-out never rewrites the user's global setting.

subject: /knowledge/plugin-conventions/hook-shell-test-harness
body: Every plugin ships a shell test harness that pipes a JSON payload to the hook on stdin and asserts on both the exit code and the emitted output shape.

subject: /knowledge/plugin-conventions/hooks-json-descriptions
body: hooks.json descriptions are written as real prose documentation of what the hook does and why, not a one-line label nobody will expand on later.

subject: /knowledge/plugin-conventions/delegation-enforcement-layer
body: Delegation to a cheaper runner is enforced at the tool-permission layer, not by instructions alone, since instructions are the first thing a model drops under pressure.

subject: /knowledge/agent-collaboration/preserve-behavior-vs-defect
body: An implementor told to preserve behavior precisely will faithfully preserve a defect along with it — state explicitly which behaviors are the contract, not just keep it working the same.

subject: /knowledge/agent-collaboration/scope-to-defect-class
body: Scoping a fix to the one file that showed the bug lets the same defect survive untouched in a sibling file — scope the fix to the defect class, not the symptom's location.

subject: /knowledge/agent-collaboration/untested-guard-is-decoration
body: A lint or guard test that has never been observed to fail is decoration, not protection, until someone deliberately breaks the rule and watches it get caught.

subject: /knowledge/agent-collaboration/exit-code-only-test
body: A test asserting only an exit code cannot distinguish an active decision from silently falling through — assert the emitted output's shape too.

subject: /knowledge/agent-collaboration/instrumentation-independence
body: Instrumentation must not depend on the same behavior it is measuring, or a failure in that behavior becomes invisible in exactly the data meant to reveal it.

subject: /knowledge/agent-collaboration/documentation-silence
body: Absence of a statement in documentation is not evidence of absence in behaviour — treat undocumented as unknown, not as ruled out, and verify by probing.

subject: /knowledge/agent-collaboration/adoption-vs-demand
body: Adoption of a tool by a model is roughly inversely proportional to what it demands of the model — passive auto-capture gets used heavily, structured authoring gets skipped.

subject: /knowledge/agent-collaboration/invisible-crashed-process
body: Low observed usage of a background or dependent process is not evidence of disinterest until a silent crash of that process has been ruled out first.

subject: /knowledge/dotnet-and-storage/filemode-append-race
body: FileMode.Append in .NET is seek-then-write, not POSIX O_APPEND, so concurrent appends can resolve the same offset and end up losing writes — unlike Node's appendFileSync, which is O_APPEND and atomic.

subject: /knowledge/dotnet-and-storage/jsonarray-add-aot
body: JsonArray.Add binds to the AOT-hostile generic overload by default; cast the array through IList<JsonNode?> first to call the non-generic Add and stay trim-safe.

subject: /knowledge/dotnet-and-storage/pragma-foreign-keys-scope
body: foreign_keys, busy_timeout and synchronous are connection-scoped, so a schema file cannot set them. Measured: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite already sends foreign_keys=1, but leaves busy_timeout=0 and synchronous=2.

subject: /knowledge/dotnet-and-storage/begin-immediate-required
body: Every SQLite write transaction should open BEGIN IMMEDIATE — a deferred transaction upgrading to a writer raises SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT, which busy_timeout cannot wait out.

subject: /knowledge/dotnet-and-storage/fts5-delete-needs-old-values
body: A SQLite FTS5 external-content table needs the previously indexed column values to evict a row — its delete command requires them, and content='table' has them by construction.

subject: /knowledge/dotnet-and-storage/atomic-rename-same-dir
body: A temp file used for an atomic rename must be created in the same directory as its target — renaming across filesystems or mount points is not atomic.

subject: /knowledge/dotnet-and-storage/fts5-external-content-columns
body: SQLite FTS5 external-content tables can only index columns that exist on the content table — a denormalized join column has to be joined at query time instead.

subject: /knowledge/dotnet-and-storage/orm-hostile-to-aot
body: An ORM or EF Core is reflection-heavy and hostile to Native AOT trimming; hand-written SQL keeps the AOT surface small and the query plans visible.
